notes: The list of what changed in an update is readable now. Every line arrived cut off mid-word with a sideways scrollbar under it, so the one thing this dialog exists to show you was the one thing you could not read.

Taking an update no longer reloads the page out from under you. It says the newer version is on your site and leaves the reload to you, so you stay signed in and whatever else was on the screen stays there.

A page you have already updated stops asking you to update it again. For a few minutes after you publish, a gateway can still hand out the copy of your page it had before, and that older copy would offer you the same update a second time. It now says the update is published and offers you a reload.
Updating no longer answers you with a list of dead links. Those are about your own pages, they were there before you pressed Update, and you will hear about them the next time you save.

The toolbar speaks the language of the page. On a Slovak, Czech or Spanish page, Write, Edit content, Settings, History and Save stayed in English beside the words that had been translated. A button you renamed yourself is left as you wrote it.

The sign-in box, the settings, the version list and this update offer come out as boxes again on a page whose own stylesheet has a rule about forms. On one site this dialog arrived as four narrow columns with its buttons pushed off the side of the screen, which made it almost impossible to read and nearly impossible to press. The content panel had the same problem on a page that styles its asides.
The box you paste a key into is now as wide as the dialog around it, rather than the small default the browser picks.

A link to a page that is not in your site no longer stops you saving. The page is published, and a panel lists the addresses that lead nowhere and stays on the screen until you close it, with a button that copies the list. Until now one link to a page that did not exist yet meant nothing could be saved at all.
A link written as /shop/ is understood to mean the page at /shop/index.html, the way any web address works, so a site with more than one page stops reporting its own links as broken.

When a save fails, the reason stays on the screen until you dismiss it and can be selected and copied. It used to vanish after two seconds, which is not long enough to read a list of file names, let alone send one to whoever can fix it.
A page that carries no content form no longer shows an Edit content button that opens nothing.
Pasting into a one-line region no longer splits it. A pasted paragraph used to nest a second <a> inside a button, which came back after the next load as two buttons with the first one empty.
A block's rail can reach inside the block. The new ⌷ button lists what a block is made of, so a stray element can be removed without deleting the block around it.
A button's link can be changed. Pressing the link button inside one used to try to put a link inside a link.
Settings says which runtime the page is running, and can move it to a newer one.
A dialog opened on top of another no longer shares its Escape key with the one underneath.

A publish that stalls now ends and says which Blossom server stopped answering, instead of sitting on "Uploading… 1/4" forever. Every network call has a timeout, and each server gets its own line with a running clock.
A blob is signed once rather than once per base64 encoding, which halves how many times a phone signer asks you to approve the same upload.
The publisher has a panel for the relays and Blossom servers it uses, so one server refusing you is something you can work around without a terminal.

A publish asks the Blossom servers what they already hold before it signs anything, so a phone signer is asked once per file rather than once per file per server, all in one burst at the start. Republishing an unchanged site now needs no upload approvals at all.
nc:watch-dom, off by default, makes any change to the page count as an edit rather than only typing.
